title: Post Malone to Headline 2026 World Cup Closing Ceremony
summary: The ceremony's previously announced lineup includes Jennifer Hudson delivering the national anthem, and more stars.
contentText:
The 2026 World Cup Final keeps getting bigger and bigger. FIFA announced on Wednesday (July 15) that Post Malone will be headlining the closing ceremony, which will take place before the game kicks off at Sunday (July 19) at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J.

How Oasis’ ‘Wonderwall’ Became the Unofficial Anthem for England’s Epic World Cup Run

FIFA teased in a press release that the set by Posty — who boasts six Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 songs and three Billboard 200 No. 1 albums to date — will “landmark performance” to lead into the final match.

“At a time when sport, culture and global attention converge, Post Malone will deliver a performance designed to celebrate the tournament’s journey and ignite the atmosphere before the world’s attention turns to the two finalists,” said Gianni Infantino, president of FIFA, in a statement. “We are thrilled to have so many stars taking to the pitch, from both the football and entertainment worlds. The closing ceremony will set the tone for a historic FIFA World Cup final, uniting the passion of 48 teams, 16 host cities and millions of fans on one unforgettable stage.”

The announcement of the 18-time Grammy nominee’s high-profile gig on the pitch comes a day after FIFA revealed that Jennifer Hudson would deliver the national anthem on the final game day, with the closing ceremony also set to feature performances from global music stars Nicole Scherzinger, Laura Pausini and Robbie Williams. Superstar Tom Cruise, as well as streamer IShowSpeed, will also be participating. The closing ceremony is scheduled to begin at 1:30 p.m. ET, which is 90 minutes before the match begins.

And as previously announced, the World Cup Final Halftime Show will feature some of the biggest stars in music. The 11-minute performance will be co-headlined by BTS, Justin Bieber, Madonna and Shakira, with the halftime set curated by Coldplay’s Chris Martin.

Spain defeated France in the Tuesday (July 14) semifinal, and will move forward to the final match. Spain’s opponent will be determined by the highly anticipated Wednesday game between England and Argentina, which kicks off at 3 p.m. ET.
